conviction_note: Each finding sized alone sums to +0.8: the negatives (FY guide/FCF arithmetic needs H2 FCF of about +$1.4bn, US HRC steel up ~40% y/y, Electrolux's -5% NA demand and trade-down, soft housing) roughly cancel against the positioning (27.3% of float short with days to cover rising, a bar cut hard through October, -5.5% on print day to a 52-week low) and peer evidence that industry pricing is holding. The scaled number is p_up 52 on abs_move 13.5 = +0.54. abs_move sits above the 12.2% event-implied move because a guidance change is near-certain (street FY $2.25 already sits below the $2.50-3.00 guide), the short is crowded, and the equity is a ~$1.7bn stub on ~$5.8bn net debt. p_up stays near 50 because the EPS bar is disputed ($0.78 / $0.93 / $1.01, with Zacks' most-accurate estimate near $0.20). The two measurements agree in sign and are small. Neither has an unpriced company-level number behind it.

Company FY2026 guide (reaffirmed operationally 2026-08-03): ongoing EPS $2.50-3.00, ongoing EBIT margin ~4%, FCF >$300m, net debt <$5.0bn at year end (https://whirlpool.mediaroom.com/2026-08-03-Whirlpool-Corporation-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results). MarketBeat street FY EPS is $2.25, below the guide's low end, so an EPS guide cut is expected. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest 17,465,715 shares = 27.33% of float, days to cover 6.0, up 12.4% from 15.53m on the 2026-09-15 settlement; record date 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/WHR/short-interest). Skew is +0.86 vol points (25d put minus call), so the option market is balanced and does not lean. Put/call OI 0.98. Event-implied move 12.21% (straddle 16.93% to the 2026-11-20 expiry). Run-up 20d -15.4%, 0.43% above the 52-week low, -71% from the 52-week high. On print day the stock was -5.5% intraday to $26.57 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/550453-why-whirlpool-corporation8217s-whr-stock-is-down-531). The short is crowded and building, so negatives are shrunk for it.

findings.finding: Direct peer Electrolux reported Q3 on 2026-10-23, after WHR last spoke on 2026-08-03. North American core-appliance demand fell ~5% in Q3, worse than the -3.4% WHR cited for Q2. Consumers are trading down to lower price points, and chemicals/resin were unhedged for the first time. On the other side, Electrolux NA sales rose +2% on price, the industry 'raised prices further', and promotions are 'far more reasonable' than the 'unreasonable price cuts' of Q4 2025. If WHR's larger price actions (>10% promotional in April plus ~4% list in July) track that, NA revenue would land near or above the -2.4% y/y consensus, while volume and mix weigh on the H2 guide. Net, this is a mixed read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NA revenue/margin has driven the last prints: Q2 (NA EBIT margin +240bp sequentially, FY reaffirmed) +13.8%; Q1 (demand -7.4%, guide cut, dividend suspended) -11.9%. Electrolux itself traded up as much as 12% intraday on this report and settled ~+2%.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed three sessions before the print. WHR's Zacks NA revenue consensus ($2,657m, -2.4%) does not look updated for peer price realisation of +2% organic. If the market had read this as price discipline, WHR would not have kept making new lows into the print. If it had read it as demand deterioration, the skew would lean to puts, and it is flat at +0.86.
findings.independence: Reuters via Euronext (https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/electrolux-reports-q3-core-profit-beat-says-north-america-weakness-persists, 2026-10-23) confirms NA +2% mainly on price and the trade-down. Same company and event, so not independent. The Brazil finding below also uses this report.

findings.finding: Competitors followed WHR's 2026 price increases through the summer, so WHR is less likely to lose share as its price lands in full in Q3: GE/Cafe/Monogram +7-11% (Jun 15), LG +6% (Jul 1), Bosch/Thermador +8-12% (Aug 1), KitchenAid +3.5-6.5% and Whirlpool ~+4% (Jul 9) on top of WHR's >10% April increase. WHR's Q2 call said only ~2/3 of the April increase landed in Q2, and that a Q3 NA margin step-up 'similar' to Q1-to-Q2 (+240bp) is 'absolutely critical'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: pricing-led sequential NA margin gain plus a reaffirmed FY bought +13.8% despite an EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The price increases are public, but consensus Q3 EPS has been cut over the last 30 days and the stock is -13% month to date, which reads as a bet that price does not stick. If the market believed it would stick, the most-accurate EPS estimate would not sit near $0.20 against a $0.78 consensus. The finding lands inside what management guided (pricing was in the plan), so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Retailer blog, not a primary document. Electrolux Q3 (a different source) says the industry 'raised prices further in the quarter' and that promotions are more rational. WHR Q2 call: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-whirlpool-misses-q2-2026-estimates-but-shares-rise-93CH-4834496

findings.finding: US retail appliance sell-through held up in the summer quarter. Best Buy's appliance comp was +0.2% (vs -9.2% a year ago), with large appliances growing, for the quarter ended 2026-08-01. Lowe's reported a seventh straight positive appliance comp in the quarter ended 2026-07-31, with ticket +2.3%. Both rest mostly on price and both periods overlap WHR's Q2 more than its Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable in the baseline. NA revenue was -1.5% in Q2 against a -3.4% industry and the stock rose +13.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The data is public and mostly pre-dates WHR's Q3. It is filed because it shows price is holding at retail, which the October estimate cuts discount. It is a proxy, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Lowe's Q2 call highlights (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/lowes-companies-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-19/, 2026-08-19), a separate retailer.

findings.finding: US hot-rolled coil reached $1,210-1,220/short ton in late September 2026 (Kallanish, 25 Sept), against $825-865 a year earlier, about +40%. Nucor raised its CSP $10/st every week through September and SMU's average approached $1,300/st. WHR said on the Q2 call that steel is 'at the high end of contracts', and Electrolux says steel is on yearly contracts now being renegotiated. That points to a 2027 cost headwind that will be visible in Q4 commentary and any early 2027 framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raw materials were cited as a headwind in Q2 (stock +13.8% anyway). Not separable as a line.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side cuts in October focus on demand and the 2026 EPS. If the market were pricing a 2027 steel reset, the 2027 street EPS ($3.33 per MarketBeat) would not still sit ~30% above the 2026 guide midpoint.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that WHR has not quantified. Electrolux's Q3 call (different company) says steel contracts are yearly and being renegotiated in a volatile market, and that raw materials and logistics rose sharply.

findings.finding: US existing-home sales for September 2026 were 3.99m SAAR, -2.2% y/y. NAR said August and September were the two slowest months of the year and that rising mortgage rates in recent weeks mean fewer buyers qualify. This is a demand proxy for the discretionary and builder part of WHR's mix.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Housing is a recurring negative cited on prints. Q1 2026 (-11.9%) carried the demand collapse.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the release is public and the stock is -15% in 20 days. Filed as a small proxy. WHR says demand is mostly replacement-driven, which limits the transmission.
findings.independence: Proxy. Electrolux's Q3 call reports US consumer confidence at a 10-year low and NA demand -5% (a different source on the same demand theme).

findings.finding: WHR's own Q2 release puts the FY guide out of reach on the cash line. H1 ongoing EPS was -$0.77 (Q1 -$0.56, Q2 -$0.21), so the $2.50-3.00 FY guide needs +$3.27-3.77 in H2. The ~$630m FY ongoing EBIT needs ~$520m in H2 against $106m in H1. FCF of 'over $300m' after H1 FCF of -$1,108m needs ~+$1.4bn in H2, yet management said it does not expect the usual heavy H2 working-capital release. Separately, the 10-Q shows supply-chain-financing payables falling from $772m to $629m, a working-capital drain. The street has already cut FY EPS to $2.25, so the EPS cut is expected. The unpriced swing is whether the FCF and the 'net debt below $5bn' target (from ~$5.8bn) are also cut, on an equity worth ~$1.7bn against that debt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance decides this name. Q1 2026 FY cut plus dividend suspension: -11.9%. Q2 2026 EPS miss with the FY operating guide and FCF reaffirmed: +13.8%. Jul 2025 guide cut: -13.4%. Jan 2025 guide: -16.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The EPS shortfall is priced: the street FY sits below the guide's low end. The FCF and net-debt targets have not been publicly cut by the street in what I could find. If the market had priced an FCF cut on a ~3.4x net-debt-to-market-cap stub, the 25-delta skew would bid puts, and it is flat at +0.86.
findings.independence: Q2 call (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-whirlpool-misses-q2-2026-estimates-but-shares-rise-93CH-4834496) for the 'no heavy H2 working-capital release' statement. 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000106640/000010664026000061/whr-20260630.htm) for supply-chain financing ($629m vs $772m) and the second-lien notes. All are company documents. Counterweight: maturities are cleared to 2028+ (second-lien notes due 2031/2034) and the $2bn ABL was undrawn at June 30, so this is a valuation risk, not a liquidity crisis. Shrunk for that and for the crowded short.

findings.finding: The bar was cut hard through October into the print. Zacks moved to Strong Sell on Oct 5 and its Q3 EPS consensus of $0.78 was cut over 30 days, with ESP -74.5% (most-accurate estimate ~$0.20). RBC cut its target to $22 (Oct 7), Citi to $32 from $48 (Oct 12) and Wells Fargo to $30 from $39 (Oct 16). The stock is -13.4% month to date and fell -5.5% on print day to $26.57, 0.4% above its 52-week low. Q2 showed the setup: a miss against a lowered bar with the FY operating guide reaffirmed bought +13.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS -$0.21 vs -$0.06 consensus and the stock +13.8%. Q4 2025 (-4.8%) and Q1 2026 (-11.9%) fell with no bar reset ahead of them.
findings.why_not_priced: The cuts are public. What is not settled is which bar the print is judged against ($0.20 / $0.78 / $0.93 / $1.01). A merely bad number can clear the lowest one, which the -5.5% print-day slide does not reflect. Capped small because the EPS bar is disputed.
findings.independence: MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-whirlpool-whr-projected-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/) for the RBC/Citi cuts. MarketBeat 2026-10-21 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-whirlpool-nyse-whr-stock-falls-57-whats-next-2026-10-21/) for Wells Fargo. AAII 2026-10-26 for the print-day drop.

That is a crowded and building short into a print where any reaffirmation of the FCF and net-debt targets, or a smaller-than-feared cut, can trigger covering. baseline_tension: The evidence is mixed and agrees with a balanced skew (+0.86). The -15% 20-day run-up and the crowded 27% short argue that the guide cut is in the price, which cuts against the negative fundamental findings and is why p_up is held at 52 rather than below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar): the EPS bar has four values ($0.20/$0.78/$0.93/$1.01), so the bar-reset finding was capped from +1.2 to +0.8 and print_vs_bar moved to the revenue bar, where three sources roughly agree.
Rule 7 (crowded short at 27% of float): shrank the negatives once each. Guide/FCF arithmetic -2.0 to -1.5, steel -1.0 to -0.7, housing -0.4 to -0.3.

'A peer's print landing after the company last spoke' plus rule 9 (net of the rest): re-read Electrolux's +2% price-led NA sales and rational promotion against WHR's -2.4% NA revenue consensus, and moved that finding from -0.8 to +0.2 net of the -5% demand. print_vs_bar went from +0.5 to +1.5.
Rule 5 (proxy): retailer comps cut from +0.3 to +0.2 because their quarters end in July. Added a near-zero LG finding rather than leaving a sourced peer fact unfiled.
'What has worked' (covenant arithmetic did not pay): kept the FCF finding at a moderate size even though it rests on company documents.
